title: APPROVAL OF FINDINGS OF FACT, STATEMENT OF OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS, AND MITIGATION MONITORING AND REPORTING PROGRAM FOR THE WEST SANTA ANA BRANCH TRANSIT CORRIDOR (ALSO KNOWN AS SOUTHEAST GATEWAY LI
text:
RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - APPROVAL OF FINDINGS OF FACT, STATEMENT OF OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS, AND MITIGATION MONITORING AND REPORTING PROGRAM FOR THE WEST SANTA ANA BRANCH TRANSIT CORRIDOR (ALSO KNOWN AS SOUTHEAST GATEWAY LINE) JOINT PORTS-OWNED SAN PEDRO SUBDIVISION RIGHT-OF-WAY (APPLICATION FOR PORT PERMIT NUMBER 240103-002; STATE CLEARINGHOUSE NO. 2017061007)
Transmittal 1
Summary
: Staff requests approval of the Findings of Fact, Statement of Overriding Considerations, and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Plan (MMRP) for the West Santa Ana Branch Transit Corridor (WSAB) Project (Project). The Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) is the lead agency for this Project. Components of the Project affect property owned jointly by the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department (Harbor Department) and the Port of Long Beach (POLB) (collectively “Ports”); therefore, the Harbor Department is a Responsible Agency under the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) (Pub. Resources Code, §21000 et seq.) and is required to take action to review environmental evaluation documents prior to administering permits. The Project is a light rail transit (LRT) line that will extend from a northern terminus in the City of Los Angeles/Florence-Firestone community of Los Angeles County to a southern terminus in the City of Artesia. Metro, as the Lead Agency under CEQA, analyzed the Project in the 2024 Final Environmental Impact Report (FEIR/EIS). The Harbor Department, as a Responsible Agency under CEQA, is required to consider Metro’s CEQA document, prior to acting on a project as a Responsible Agency pursuant to the process described in the Guidelines for CEQA (“CEQA Guidelines”) (California Code of Regulations, Title 14, §15096). For the Project to be completed, the Harbor Department, in its role as a Responsible Agency, would be required to issue real estate entitlement(s) in the form of one or more Joint Revocable Permits, a Master Joint Revocable Permit, construction entitlements, and long-term conveyance or easement to Metro. The proposed action is in alignment with Strategic Objective 4: Strong Relationships with Stakeholders.
Recommendation
: Board resolve to 1) find that Metro’s Project requires real estate transactions, permitting and relocation of freight tracks on the San Pedro Subdivision right-of-way, which is jointly owned by the City of Los Angeles and the City of Long Beach; 2) find that the real estate transactions, permitting and relocation of freight tracks on the San Pedro Subdivision right-of-way require environmental review under the provisions of CEQA; 3) find that the Final EIR/EIS for the Project prepared by Metro, which included a Statement of Overriding Considerations and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program, was certified by Metro as compliant with CEQA; 4) find that the Harbor Department, as a Responsible Agency under CEQA, has independently reviewed Metro’s Final EIR/EIS for the Project; 5) adopt the Findings of Fact and Statement of Overriding Considerations; 6) adopt the mitigation measures contained in the Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program that pertain to the construction occurring on Harbor Department property of the certified Final Environmental Impact Report; 7) find that other than those mitigation measures required or incorporated pursuant to the Final EIS/EIR for the Project by Metro, there are no feasible mitigation measures within the Harbor Department’s jurisdiction which could be adopted at this time, which would avoid or significantly mitigate those significant, potentially significant, or cumulatively considerable adverse environmental impacts identified the Final EIS/EIR; 8) authorize the Environmental Management Division to file the Notice of Determination with the Los Angeles County Clerk and the State Clearinghouse; and 9) adopt Resolution No. ______________.
summary: Adopts CEQA findings and an overriding-considerations statement so the Harbor Department can issue property permits and easements for Metro's light rail line along the jointly owned San Pedro Subdivision rail right-of-way.
